title: Launchpad: Traffic routing onboarding & version lockup quickstart visuals
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design quickstart assets and screenshots for the Launchpad onboarding flow that teaches customers how to configure release traffic routing (canary/A-B), set version locks, and define fallback policies. Includes step-by-step guided screens, explainer illustrations, and simulated traffic preview to reduce time-to-first-safe-deploy.
acceptance_criteria: Assets include hi-fi mockups for desktop and tablet of 4 core screens: 'Create Release', 'Traffic Split Editor', 'Version Lock Details', and 'Fallback Policy Composer'.
Illustration set (3) explaining canary, A/B, and fallback behavior in under 30s each for documentation embedding.
Annotated screenshot pack with copy for microcopy, tooltips, and error states (unauthorized, conflicting locks, capacity limit).
Prototype in Figma with interactive traffic simulator that mirrors Console routing logic and supports toggles for Dedicated/Private environments.
Exported assets as PNGs, SVG icons, and a single-page onboarding PDF for marketing collateral.
design_notes: Visual language uses existing Launchpad tokens: token-primary=#0B66FF, token-warning=#FFB74D, token-success=#22C55E.
Traffic editor uses a draggable dual-handle slider with percentage chips. Show instantaneous cost & latency delta estimate when adjusting splits.
Version lock UI shows semantic version badge, commit hash, and 'pin source' badge (UI: API | Console | CI).
Fallback composer supports rule layers: capacity threshold, error rate, latency spike. Each rule has contextual helper copy and examples.
Accessible color contrast checked at 4.5:1 for primary CTA and 3.0:1 for supplementary chips; provide alternative dashed pattern for color-blind users.
Export artboards at 1440x900 and 1024x768; provide retina 2x PNGs and SVG for vector diagrams.
decisions: Use single combined 'Traffic Split' screen rather than separate canary/editor screens to reduce context switching (favored by PM and Eng).
Simulator shows deterministic synthetic traffic with seeded user journeys for predictable preview rather than sampling live traffic for privacy reasons.
Fallback policy composer will allow 3 rule layers initially to simplify UX; we will revisit after telemetry shows demand for more complex rules.
Microcopy will avoid jargon like 'KV cache' and use 'session memory' in onboarding examples per UX writing guidance.
feedback: PM (Jin Seo): prefer clearer distinction between 'version lock' and 'pin' in copy — update header to 'Version Lock (pin to this release)'.
ENG (Ravi Menon): requested inclusion of 'capacity signals' visualization to match Dedicated autoscaling behavior; added latency/cost delta mock.
Security (Lina Gomez): flagged that exportable PDF should redact internal model IDs unless customer opts-in; added opt-out checkbox on export modal.
Design Review (Nora Blake): suggested increasing size of traffic slider handles for touch targets and adding keyboard shortcut hints.
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi screens and handoff tokens to engineering UI kit (due 2026-03-18).
Create short 30s animated explainer clips for docs embedding (motion design ticket DES-93602).
Implement accessibility QA with QA team and schedule a design-dev sync to review edge error states (2026-03-20).
Prepare release screenshot pack and onboarding PDF for Launchpad beta release notes (release: console-2026.04).
